props.name: labels
props.description: Writes the value at the end of every bar (default `false`)

props.name: deep
props.description:
Also follows in-place mutations of nested data (`series[0].data.push()`);
by default the chart updates when a prop is replaced (cheaper on large data)

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stacks the series on top of each other (default `false`)

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static (default `true`)

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D (default `auto`)

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels (default `100%`)

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels, strings any CSS length

props.name: series
props.description: Data series (replace the array or a `data` array to update the chart)

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale of the texts and numbers the engine writes (tooltip, axes, accessible names); the page language by default

<script setup lang="ts">
// <HorizontalBarChart>: categories down the left side, long names stay
// readable; `labels` writes the value at the end of every bar.
import { computed } from "vue";
import { useI18n } from "minerva-design/vue";
import { HorizontalBarChart } from "minerva-design/vue/charts";

const TEXT = {
  en: {
    views: "Page views",
    pages: ["Home", "Pricing", "Documentation", "Blog", "Careers", "Contact"],
  },
  zh: {
    views: "浏览量",
    pages: ["首页", "价格", "文档", "博客", "招聘", "联系我们"],
  },
  ja: {
    views: "ページビュー",
    pages: [
      "ホーム",
      "料金",
      "ドキュメント",
      "ブログ",
      "採用情報",
      "お問い合わせ",
    ],
  },
  fr: {
    views: "Pages vues",
    pages: [
      "Accueil",
      "Tarifs",
      "Documentation",
      "Blog",
      "Carrières",
      "Contact",
    ],
  },
};

const VIEWS = [48200, 31900, 27400, 15800, 9100, 4300];

const { language } = useI18n();
const series = computed(() => {
  const text = TEXT[language.value] ?? TEXT.en;
  return [
    {
      name: text.views,
      data: VIEWS.map((y, i) => ({ x: text.pages[i], y })),
    },
  ];
});
</script>

<template>
  <HorizontalBarChart
    :series="series"
    :x-axis="{ type: 'category' }"
    labels
    :height="300"
  />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
// `stacked percent`: every row adds up to 100 %, a survey answered on a
// three-point scale; the legend toggles an answer.
import { computed } from "vue";
import { useI18n } from "minerva-design/vue";
import { HorizontalBarChart } from "minerva-design/vue/charts";

const TEXT = {
  en: {
    answers: ["Agree", "Neutral", "Disagree"],
    questions: [
      "Easy to set up",
      "Good documentation",
      "Fast enough",
      "Would recommend",
    ],
  },
  zh: {
    answers: ["同意", "中立", "不同意"],
    questions: ["易于上手", "文档完善", "速度够快", "愿意推荐"],
  },
  ja: {
    answers: ["そう思う", "どちらでもない", "そう思わない"],
    questions: [
      "導入が簡単",
      "ドキュメントが充実",
      "十分に速い",
      "人に勧めたい",
    ],
  },
  fr: {
    answers: ["D’accord", "Neutre", "Pas d’accord"],
    questions: [
      "Facile à installer",
      "Bonne documentation",
      "Assez rapide",
      "Je recommande",
    ],
  },
};

// answers per question: agree, neutral, disagree
const ANSWERS = [
  [72, 18, 10],
  [58, 27, 15],
  [64, 21, 15],
  [81, 12, 7],
];
const palette = [
  "var(--success-color, #16a34a)",
  "var(--text-secondary-color, #9ca3af)",
  "var(--danger-color, #dc2626)",
];

const { language } = useI18n();
const series = computed(() => {
  const text = TEXT[language.value] ?? TEXT.en;
  return text.answers.map((name, k) => ({
    name,
    data: text.questions.map((x, i) => ({ x, y: ANSWERS[i][k] })),
  }));
});
</script>

<template>
  <HorizontalBarChart
    :series="series"
    :x-axis="{ type: 'category' }"
    :palette="palette"
    stacked
    percent
    :height="260"
  />
</template>

translationResources.title: Horizontal bar chart
translationResources.description: Bars growing from the left with the categories down the side: rankings, long names, diverging surveys and progress.

basic.title: Ranking
basic.description: The categories run from top to bottom in data order, so a sorted list reads as a ranking; labels writes the value at the end of every bar.

diverging.title: Diverging survey
diverging.description: Negative values grow to the left of zero: a stacked Likert scale puts disagreement on the left and agreement on the right, the axis format shows both sides as positive shares.

progress.title: Stacked progress
progress.description: percent fills every row to 100%: the status of the issues of each team, while the tooltip keeps the counts.

long-labels.title: Long labels
long-labels.description: Long category names stay readable on the left: the axis takes the width of the longest name instead of rotating the labels.

grouped.title: Grouped
grouped.description: Several series sit side by side in each row, here the budget and the actual spend of every department.

negative.title: Positive and negative
negative.description: Each datum sets its color; labels of negative bars are written on their left side.

top-n.title: Top N
top-n.description: A RadioGroup picks the metric and a Select how many rows to keep: the data is sorted and cut before it reaches the chart, and the height follows the number of rows. The output gives the share of the total that the top rows make.

race.title: Bar chart race
race.description: A setInterval, cleared on pause and on unmount, interpolates the installed solar capacity between year ends and re-sorts the rows at every step. Each country keeps its datum color while it moves, and Intl.DisplayNames writes its name.

salary-bands.title: Salary bands
salary-bands.description: Floating bars go from y0 to y: the salary band of each job level. A y line annotation follows the offer set with the buttons, the bands that contain it turn green, and renderTooltip shows the minimum, midpoint, maximum and compa-ratio.

error-budget.title: Error budgets
error-budget.description: The error budget left to each service, worst first, colored by threshold; overspent budgets grow to the left of zero. onPointClick writes the SLO, the measured availability and the downtime minutes left in an output, and onPlotClick clears it.

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Tap a bar: onPointClick receives the app and its users; labels writes the values at the bar ends.

HorizontalBarChartProps.series: Series drawn as bars from the left unless they set a type; the categories run from top to bottom
HorizontalBarChartProps.labels: Writes the value at the end of every bar

ranking.title: Most visited pages
ranking.description: Categories down the left side keep long names readable; labels write the value at the end of every bar.

survey.title: Survey answers, 100 % stacked
survey.description: Stacked and percent: every row adds up to 100 %; click a legend item to hide an answer.

props.stacked: Stacks the bars of every series instead of grouping them
props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
